paragraphs.title: Abijah's Illness and Ahijah's Prophecy against Jeroboam's House

easy.explanation: The first verse says that Abijah the son of Jeroboam fell sick.
easy.q: Who became sick at the beginning of the account?

easy.explanation: Jeroboam sent her to Shiloh to see Ahijah the prophet.
easy.q: To whom was Jeroboam's wife sent?

answers: Disguise herself so she would not be recognized
easy.explanation: Jeroboam told her to disguise herself as another woman.
easy.q: What did Jeroboam tell his wife to do?

answers: Ten loaves, cracknels, and a cruse of honey
A sword and a message from the king
medium.explanation: Jeroboam told her to take ten loaves, cracknels, and a cruse of honey.
medium.q: What did Jeroboam's wife take with her to Ahijah?

answers: The Lord told him that Jeroboam's wife was coming
medium.explanation: The Lord revealed to Ahijah that Jeroboam's wife was coming disguised.
medium.q: How did Ahijah know who she was even though he could not see?

answers: All the males of Jeroboam's household
medium.explanation: The expression refers broadly to the males of Jeroboam's house, from the least to the greatest.
medium.q: In the prophecy, what does “him that pisseth against the wall” refer to?

answers: Some good thing toward the Lord was found in him
challenge.explanation: The Lord said that Abijah alone would come to the grave because some good thing was found in him.
challenge.q: Why would Abijah receive a grave and mourning unlike the rest of Jeroboam's house?

answers: Jeroboam sinned and made Israel to sin
Israel sinned without any connection to Jeroboam
The punishment was caused only by Abijah's illness
challenge.explanation: The prophecy says Israel would be given up because of Jeroboam's sins, by which he made Israel sin.
challenge.q: What connection does the prophecy make between Jeroboam's sins and Israel's punishment?

answers: Jeroboam's wife returned, and the child died
challenge.explanation: When Jeroboam's wife came to the threshold at Tirzah, the child died.
challenge.q: What happened after Ahijah delivered the prophecy?

easy.explanation: The KJV says that Jeroboam reigned two and twenty years.
easy.q: How many years did Jeroboam reign?

easy.explanation: After Jeroboam died, Nadab his son reigned in his stead.

answers: His wars and the other acts of his reign
easy.explanation: The chapter refers to the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel for his wars and acts.
easy.q: What does the chapter say is recorded elsewhere about Jeroboam?

medium.explanation: This expression is a customary biblical way of saying that Jeroboam died.
medium.q: What does “he slept with his fathers” mean in this passage?

answers: The account of his son Nadab reigning in his stead
An account of a campaign in Egypt
A description of new high places
medium.explanation: The next statement says that Nadab his son reigned in his stead.
medium.q: What follows the summary of Jeroboam's reign?

answers: To say that Jeroboam never reigned
medium.explanation: The reference indicates that further details about Jeroboam are recorded elsewhere.
medium.q: Why does the chapter mention the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

answers: His acts and wars, the length of his reign, his death, and his successor
His birth, marriage, and journey to Egypt
His building projects, offerings, and coronation
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions his acts and wars, twenty-two years of reign, his death, and Nadab as successor.
challenge.q: Which pattern summarizes the end of Jeroboam's reign?

answers: The chapter records every detail of Jeroboam's life
The chapter gives a summary and points to a fuller record
There is no information about Jeroboam
challenge.explanation: The chapter summarizes major facts and directs the reader to another record for more details.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the reference to additional chronicles?

answers: Both accounts describe a king's reign and successor
Both accounts focus only on the temple
There is no transition between the two kings
challenge.explanation: After describing Jeroboam's death and successor, the chapter turns to Rehoboam's reign.
challenge.q: How does the end of Jeroboam's account lead into the account of Rehoboam?

paragraphs.title: Rehoboam's Reign and Judah's Religious Decline

easy.explanation: Rehoboam reigned in Judah, in Jerusalem.
The passage says that Judah did evil in the sight of the Lord.
easy.q: How is Judah's conduct described in the sight of the Lord?

easy.explanation: The KJV mentions high places, images, and groves.
easy.q: What did the people build on the high hills and under the green trees?

answers: Sacred trees or symbols connected with foreign worship
medium.explanation: The groves are listed with high places and images as part of forbidden worship.

answers: Judah followed the abominations of the nations
The nations learned their practices from Judah
medium.explanation: Judah did according to the abominations of the nations whom the Lord had cast out.
medium.q: How does the passage compare Judah's actions with those of the nations?

medium.explanation: These practices show that the people were turning away from the Lord.
medium.q: What conclusion follows from the presence of high places, images, and groves?

answers: Both led their people into war
Both involved turning away from the Lord and forbidden worship
challenge.explanation: Both accounts describe practices that provoked the Lord and led people away from faithful worship.
challenge.q: What is the main similarity between Judah's sins and Jeroboam's sins in this chapter?

answers: It emphasizes the contrast between the holy place and Judah's evil actions
It explains why Rehoboam moved to Shiloh
It proves that Rehoboam was not king
challenge.explanation: The sacred city is contrasted with the sinful practices carried out during Rehoboam's reign.
challenge.q: Why is Jerusalem's description as the city chosen for the Lord's name significant here?

answers: He did not prevent the decline described
He abolished the kingdom of Judah
challenge.explanation: The passage records Judah's evil without saying that Rehoboam opposed or stopped it.
challenge.q: What can be inferred about Rehoboam's leadership from the description of Judah's decline?

paragraphs.title: Shishak's Campaign and the Loss of Jerusalem's Treasures

answers: In the fifth year of King Rehoboam
In the seventeenth year of his reign
easy.explanation: The passage says that Shishak came in the fifth year of King Rehoboam.
easy.q: When did Shishak king of Egypt come against Jerusalem?

answers: The treasures of the Lord's house, the king's house, and Solomon's gold shields
Only the books of the law
easy.explanation: Shishak took the treasures of both houses and all the gold shields Solomon had made.
easy.q: What did Shishak take from Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: Rehoboam made brasen, or bronze, shields in place of the gold shields.
easy.q: What material was used for the replacement shields?

answers: Each time the king entered the Lord's house
When the king went out to war
medium.explanation: The phrase introduces the repeated royal ceremony involving the shields.
medium.q: What does the phrase “when the king went into the house of the Lord” describe?

answers: Carried them before the king and returned them to the guard chamber
Placed them in the people's house
medium.explanation: The guard carried the shields when the king entered and brought them back afterward.
medium.q: What did the guard do with the bronze shields?

answers: The loss of treasure and the kingdom's diminished condition
medium.explanation: The replacement of gold with bronze highlights the loss and impoverishment caused by the raid.
medium.q: What does the change from gold shields to bronze shields emphasize?

answers: It follows the description of Judah's evil
It occurred before Rehoboam became king
It occurred after Rehoboam's father died
challenge.explanation: The campaign is described after the chapter records Judah's sinful practices.
challenge.q: How does Shishak's campaign fit into the chapter's sequence of events?

answers: The ceremony continued even though the shields were less valuable
challenge.explanation: The ceremony remained, but bronze shields replaced the stolen gold ones.
challenge.q: What does the return of the shields to the guard chamber show about the royal ceremony?

answers: Solomon's gold shields and Rehoboam's bronze shields
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts the gold shields made by Solomon with the bronze shields made by Rehoboam.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in the account of the shields?

paragraphs.title: The End of Rehoboam's Reign and the Conflict with Jeroboam

easy.explanation: The passage says there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their days.
easy.q: Between whom was there war all their days?

easy.explanation: Rehoboam was buried with his fathers in the city of David.
Abijam his son reigned in his stead.

answers: The additional deeds and events of Rehoboam's reign
The words of Ahijah the prophet
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to further details recorded in the chronicles of the kings of Judah.
medium.q: What does “the rest of the acts of Rehoboam” mean?

answers: The war lasted only one day
medium.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the conflict continued throughout their reigns.
medium.q: What does the phrase “all their days” show about the war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam?

answers: Rehoboam's burial, the war, and then his reign
A reference to the chronicles, the war, Rehoboam's death and burial, and Abijam's reign
Abijam's reign, Shishak's campaign, and then Rehoboam's death
medium.explanation: The chapter refers to the records, mentions the war, describes Rehoboam's death and burial, and names his successor.
medium.q: What is the order of events at the end of the chapter?

answers: It describes an ongoing war between the kings of the two realms
It describes the reunification of the two kingdoms
It says both kingdoms received one king
challenge.explanation: The continuing war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam reflects the separation and conflict between the two kingdoms.
challenge.q: How does the end of the chapter reinforce the division between Israel and Judah?

answers: Both died and were succeeded by their sons
Both lost their kingdoms on the same day
challenge.explanation: Nadab succeeded Jeroboam, and Abijam succeeded Rehoboam.
challenge.q: What similarity appears in the endings of Jeroboam's and Rehoboam's reigns?

answers: It connects the account of his death with the summary of his life
It announces that she became queen
challenge.explanation: The repeated detail identifies Rehoboam's family as part of the closing account of his death and burial.
challenge.q: Why does the chapter repeat the name of Rehoboam's mother at the end?
